title: Lumina pilot weekly: circuit breaker & routing review
summary: Weekly POC sync for Lumina private pilot. Main focus: intermittent 5xxs seen during high-concurrency workloads, new circuit-breaker routing rule tested, kernel upgrade scheduled but rolled back on Friday in canary due to compatibility with patched quant kernels. Discussed MTU/fragmentation suspicion on VPC peering, TLS termination patterns, and KV cache warm-up behavior. Action items include gathering packet captures, running the Redwood perf harness at 2x concurrency, and a follow-up deep dive with Lumina NetEng and Redwood SE for routing trace analysis.
topics: circuit-breaker routing rule behavior and metrics
kernel/quantization upgrade status and rollback rationale
KV cache/prefix warm-up effects on latency
security/audit log access for pilot telemetry
action_items: Marco Silva - provide tcpdump / packet captures from two failure windows (due 2025-06-19)
Ethan Chu - run Redwood perf harness at configured 2x target concurrency and upload results to shared sheet (due 2025-06-18)
Noah Rivera - share updated telemetry dashboard links and short guide to interpreting p95/p99 for model route (due 2025-06-20)
Priya Desai - confirm KMS key rotation schedule and share rotation policy doc (due 2025-06-24)
Maya Patel - schedule routing trace deep-dive with Lumina NetEng and Redwood networking SEs (proposed 2025-06-19)
Jon Reyes - collect and share application side logs correlated with request IDs for three failure examples (due 2025-06-19)
next_steps: Run 2x concurrency perf run and compare p50/p95/p99 to last week's baseline
Packet captures + routing trace to identify MTU or fragmentation issues across VPC peering
Canary kernel upgrade postponed; plan lower-impact test matrix before next canary window
Redwood to produce short note on circuit-breaker thresholds used and suggested tuning
Follow-up deep-dive meeting with NetEng + SEs scheduled after packet capture review
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel (AE): All right folks, thanks for joining. We're here for the weekly Lumina pilot sync, focus on the error spikes and the routing rule test. Anyone new on the call?
[00:12] Dr. Aisha Khan: hi, no new folks, thanks. we had another 5xx cluster on thursday around 10:14, which is what prompted this.
[00:20] Marco Silva (NetEng): yes, started seeing head-of-line timeouts and some fragmentation-looking drops, we grabbed a couple pcaps.
[00:31] Ethan Chu (SE): ok can you confirm whether the failures were all to the same model route or multiple?
[00:40] Jon Reyes (SRE): mostly to the rtr-prod-1 route, small handful to rtr-prod-2, but rtr-prod-1 hit p99 latency spikes then 502s.
[00:53] Maya: thanks. quick status: we tested the new circuit-breaker routing rule yesterday in canary with 10% traffic, it held for small bursts but we saw a higher-than-expected fail-open count when KV cache wasn't warmed.
[01:08] Priya Desai (Security): side note on audit logs — we still need read access to the pilot telemetry in the console for our compliance review.
[01:18] Noah Rivera (CSM): noted, I'll send the minimal access role token today.
[01:24] [01:30] Ethan: so about the fail-open — that's where the rule decided to route to the fallback variant instead of cutting the circuit, right? our logs show a couple attempts to fallback to a smaller-quant model which then returned higher token times.
[01:42] Marco: correct, and then after the fallback the client retried and that maybe magnified the total concurrent in-flight requests. there's likely a retry amplification pattern.
[01:54] Aisha: we also saw a lot of TLS renegotiation on the edge during that window, could be unrelated but worth checking.
[02:05] Ethan: hmm TLS renegotiation could point to session timeouts or reverse proxy mismatch; i'll add that to the checklist.
[02:14] Maya: quick update on the kernel upgrade — the Friday canary had to be rolled back because one of the patched kernels caused rounding differences with our quantized checkpoint loader, so we reverted.
[02:30] Marco: that aligns with the timing, after the rollback we saw fewer errors but the latency didn't immediately normalize.
[02:39] Jon: we correlated the errors with a 10–15% increase in retransmits on the peering link.
[02:46] Ethan: retransmits could be MTU/fragmentation. what's the MTU on your VPC peering?
[02:52] Marco: default 1500, but some hop devices have jumbo enabled to 9000 on the transit path; may be a mismatch.
[03:01] Aisha: also, one datapoint — our health checks were flapping briefly because the probe looks for a 200 within 500ms and during the spike the p50 was 450ms but p99 shot to 3.2s.
[03:15] Maya: ok that's useful. two threads: network layer (MTU/retransmits/TCP) and application/runtime layer (KV cache warm, quant load differences).
[03:26] [03:30] Ethan: on KV cache, we noticed cold-start tokens added ~120ms per request until prefix caching warmed after roughly 40k tokens total. under high concurrency that multiplied.
[03:41] Marco: so in a retry storm the warmed cache path is not always present and you'll hit the slower code path.
[03:49] Noah: sounds like we should set a short circuit-breaker to reject early and let client backoff instead of fallback that triggers retries.
[03:58] Priya: from a security/compliance stance, we also want to ensure rollbacks are captured in audit logs and that the rollback reason is recorded — that helps for our SOC2 evidence.
[04:11] Maya: agreed, we'll include a rollback note in the telemetry event. Noah will own that.
[04:17] [04:20] Jon: question — can Redwood surface the exact request IDs that hit the fallback so we can match them to app logs?
[04:28] Ethan: yes we can. we put request_id in the response header for canary routes; we'll compile a sample set for you.
[04:34] Aisha: great, that will speed correlation.
[04:37] [05:00] Marco: another suspicion — we had an intermediate firewall with MSS clamping turned on; that can cause fragmentation. We can test disabling MSS clamping in a staging path.
[05:12] Ethan: good idea. also i want to highlight that the circuit-breaker threshold we used was relatively loose: 30 errors per minute with a 60s window; we can try tightening to 10 errors per minute and see effect.
[05:25] Maya: let's capture two configs: current (30/60) and proposed (10/60) and run the perf harness.
[05:34] Noah: i'll coordinate the harness timing with Lumina's perf window.
[05:39] [06:00] Priya: on KMS — during the kernel upgrade the container restarted a few times and we want to make sure there were no failed key lookups. our KMS team will verify.
[06:10] Ethan: there were no KMS errors surfaced on our side, but we'll ask Priya's team to check for any transient DENIED events.
[06:19] Marco: back to the packet captures — are we comfortable sharing pcaps with Redwood? they contain internal host IPs.
[06:28] Maya: we can accept them over the secure s3 bucket with the pre-signed link; we also have an NDA that covers this pilot.
[06:34] Aisha: ok we'll upload to the link you share.
[06:38] [07:00] Jon: quick ask — can Redwood add a telemetry column for whether a request hit fallback vs circuit-tripped? right now it's a single event code.
[07:10] Ethan: we can add a small flag in the next telemetry push; it'll be in the event envelope as fallback=true/false.
[07:17] Maya: perfect. also please add the model_variant name so we know which quantized path was used.
[07:25] Ethan: yes included.
[07:28] [08:00] Marco: ok timeline — we'll grab the pcaps and app logs for the two windows (10:14 and 10:52), upload by Thursday morning.
[08:10] Noah: and Redwood will run the 2x perf harness overnight Wednesday and post results.
[08:17] Aisha: on the canary kernel — any plan to do a narrower matrix? the full patch caused unexpected quant loader behavior.
[08:27] Maya: yes the new plan is smaller matrix: build with patched kernel but test only the smallest batch sizes and single-model routes first, then expand. we'll also include quant decoding tolerances.
[08:38] Ethan: and we will instrument more fine-grained metrics on the quant loader paths to catch rounding anomalies.
[08:47] [09:00] Priya: for compliance we need the timeline of the rollback and the reason recorded. can you add a one-pager?
[09:07] Maya: yes i'll produce a brief postmortem note and attach it to the ticket.
[09:13] Jon: on the routing side, we should consider adding a short-lived egress-only path to route traffic through a transit node that does MSS disabled so we can A/B test fragmentation effect.
[09:27] Marco: we can spin up that path in staging within a day, no config drift expected.
[09:33] [10:00] Ethan: technical note — when fallback occurs we see 2x token decode time on the smaller-quant model due to slower fused kernels; so fallback can actually worsen latency in some profiles.
[10:13] Aisha: good to know — that explains the user-facing error reports.
[10:18] Maya: so recommended mitigation short-term: tighten circuit-breaker, suppress automatic client retries for fallback, and ensure prefix cache warm-up (preload) before load test.
[10:31] Noah: i'll include preload scripts in the pilot repo.
[10:36] [12:00] Marco: one more thing — we noticed occasional TCP RSTs coming from a middlebox; unclear if it's health-check logic. we'll include that in the pcap.
[12:12] Ethan: ok we will look for RST sequences and retransmit patterns.
[12:18] Priya: any security concerns about the preload causing token leakage? like if we preload prefixes from sensitive prompts.
[12:28] Maya: preload will use synthetic prompts or redacted tokens, not customer data. we'll provide a preload template.
[12:38] Aisha: thanks.
[12:42] [13:00] Jon: logistics — when can we reconvene after packet analysis?
[13:07] Maya: propose Friday 10am PT; that gives everyone time to gather pcaps and run the perf harness.
[13:13] Marco: friday 10 works.
[13:17] Noah: i'll send the invite and link to the shared sheet.
[13:21] [13:30] Ethan: quick follow-up on metrics — what baseline should we compare to? last week's Wednesday run at 1200 RPS with p95 340ms?
[13:34] Aisha: yes that was baseline. our health-probe threshold is 500ms.
[13:39] Maya: ok we'll compare p50/p95/p99 to that baseline.
[13:45] [14:00] Priya: and for SOC2 evidence we want the access logs and audit events for any change; is Redwood able to provide exportable CSVs?
[14:08] Ethan: yes, we have export in the console; i'll provide an export of the last 14 days.
[14:15] Maya: thanks. any other blockers?
[14:18] [14:30] Aisha: nothing else from our side.
[14:36] Maya: recap — Marco upload pcaps, Jon and Aisha correlate app logs to request IDs, Ethan run perf harness and flag fallback request IDs, Noah share telemetry dashboard & access, Priya confirm KMS rotation details, Maya will write rollback one-pager and schedule Friday deep-dive.
[14:56] [15:00] Ethan: one small note — we'll also include a short note on recommended circuit-breaker thresholds per concurrency tier, that should help you tune quickly.
[15:08] Maya: great; thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and confirm Friday invite. meeting adjourned.
